features.name: counterarg_cognitive_complexity_mean
features.definition: On average, how cognitively complex (differentiating multiple considerations or perspectives and integrating them, with nuance or qualification) are the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Read only OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Parse the list. Rate each comment's own reasoning for cognitive complexity on a 1-5 scale: 1 = single simple assertion or one-sided/absolutist claim, no reasoning; 2 = one reason, little qualification; 3 = several distinct considerations or some qualification/acknowledgement of alternatives; 4 = explicitly differentiates multiple perspectives, conditions or trade-offs and relates them; 5 = integrates multiple perspectives into a coherent, nuanced higher-level synthesis. Judge the commenter's own assertions; quoted text from others counts only if the commenter adopts it. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, thanks-for-changing-my-view text, and reports of the outcome as evidence of complexity; if a comment contains only such content, exclude it from the mean. Return the arithmetic mean of ratings across the remaining comments. Empty list or no rateable comments: null; malformed input: null.

h0: counterarg_cognitive_complexity_mean has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view.
h1: Higher counterarg_cognitive_complexity_mean is associated with a higher likelihood that the OP changed their view.
note: No cognitive complexity definition was supplied; operationalized as a 1-5 LLM rubric (differentiation/integration) averaged over comments, which is an assumption. The mean is over all available comments with no weighting. Comment order and timing are unknown, and comments may include post-outcome text; announcements are excluded semantically. The test describes association only, not causal effect. Association is tested with an OLS linear probability model.
